reading.text:
Reading of def:Dissertation.WellPosedness.Enlarged.enlJoint.

Paper notion (Section 2): "The filtration (F_t) is the usual augmentation of the one generated by
W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0"; the PRP "passes to the independent initial
enlargement by F_0 in the standard way". So the paper's filtration is
  F_t = usual augmentation of ( F_0 v sigma(W_s, s <= t) v sigma(N(B) : B in B([0,t]) x E) ),
with F_0 independent of (W, N). The usual conditions: complete (contains all P-null sets of F)
and right-continuous. (For Levy-type drivers the null-set completion of the natural filtration is
already right-continuous; augmenting the F_0-enlarged one likewise.)

"enlJoint" by its name is the enlarged joint filtration: the joint (W,N) filtration enlarged by
the initial sigma-field F_0 (and possibly augmented). Faithful Lean definition: a filtration
indexed by time t (in [0,T] or R_+) whose t-th sigma-algebra is generated by F_0, by W_s for
s <= t, and by the counts N((0,s] x A) for s <= t and A in E (A of finite nu measure suffices, or
N restricted to [0,t] x E), together with the P-null sets (and right-continuity, if not
automatic). If the Lean object omits the augmentation, it is the "generated by" filtration, the
paper's object before augmentation; used where the paper uses (F_t) (PRP, adaptedness), the
missing augmentation would matter only if right-continuity/completeness were used. It must
contain F_0 at t = 0, must not include future information, and must use the same W and N as the
equations.

comparison.text:
def:Dissertation.WellPosedness.Enlarged.enlJoint (Enlarged/Filtration.lean:78-82):
  enlJoint 𝒢₀ D h𝒢₀ := Brownian.augFiltration (initJoint 𝒢₀ D h𝒢₀).rightCont P,
augFiltration ℱ μ t := aug (ℱ (max t 0)) mΩ μ (LevyStochCalc/Brownian/AugmentedFiltration.lean:53),
aug m mΩ μ := {A ∈ mΩ : ∃ B ∈ m, μ(A ∆ B) = 0} (Probability/Augmentation.lean:45), rightCont the
Mathlib right-continuous version (⨅_{j>i} ℱ_j), initJoint t = D.filtration t ⊔ 𝒢₀ with
D.filtration t = σ(W_s, s ≤ t) ∨ σ(N(B), B ⊆ (−∞,t] × E) (joint natural filtration).
Against the reading: F_t = augmentation by the P-null sets of ∩_{s>t}(F^{W,N}_s ∨ 𝒢₀): the usual
augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and 𝒢₀ (right-continuous version then
augmented; equal to "augment then right-continuous" by the standard lemma). Contains 𝒢₀ at time 0
(le_enlJoint_zero), the joint filtration at every time, every null set at time 0, and is right-
continuous (isRightContinuous_enlJoint). The independence of 𝒢₀ from the driver is not part of
the definition but a hypothesis (hind₀) wherever the filtration is used as the paper's, as in
Solution/ex55Linear. Representation choices: (1) augmentation by the P-null sets of mΩ inside mΩ
(Lean filtrations are sub-σ-algebras of mΩ), which is the paper's usual augmentation when
(Ω, F, P) is complete and otherwise its trace on mΩ; (2) time index ℝ, frozen at its time-0 value
for t ≤ 0; neither affects [0,T].
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
enlJoint is the usual augmentation of t ↦ F^{W,N}_t ∨ 𝒢₀: its right-continuous version, augmented
at each time by the P-null sets. Choices: (1) the null sets added are those of the ambient σ-algebra
mΩ (a Lean filtration lives inside mΩ), which is the paper's augmentation when the basis is
complete, as the paper's usual conditions assume; (2) right-continuation before augmentation,
equivalent to the usual order; (3) time runs over ℝ with the time-0 field for t ≤ 0; (4)
independence of 𝒢₀ from (W, N) is a separate hypothesis of the users, as in the paper's setting.
